title: Sarazm at its height
description: The farming town on the Zeravshan is a centre of metalworking and long-distance trade, the oldest known town in Central Asia.

title: Alexandria Eschate
description: Fighting the Sogdians, Alexander the Great founds Alexandria Eschate, his farthest city, beside the Syr Darya; it becomes today's Khujand.

title: Devashtich executed
description: The last Sogdian ruler of Panjakent is captured on Mount Mug and executed by the Arabs, completing the loss of Sogdian independence.

title: Death of Rudaki
description: The Samanid court poet Rudaki, honoured by Tajiks as the father of Persian poetry, dies blind and poor in his home village.

title: Mongols besiege Khujand
description: Timur Malik holds out against the Mongol army on an island in the Syr Darya before escaping, as Genghis Khan's conquest overruns Transoxiana.

title: Russians take Khujand
description: A Russian column storms the Bukhara-held citadel of Khujand, starting the annexation of what is now northern Tajikistan.

title: Pamir boundary fixed
description: An Anglo-Russian commission awards most of the Pamirs to Russia and leaves the Wakhan corridor to Afghanistan, ending the Great Game in the high mountains.

title: Basmachi take Dushanbe
description: Guerrillas of the Basmachi revolt drive the Bolsheviks out of the former Bukharan east, the high-water mark of resistance to Soviet rule.

title: Enver Pasha killed
description: The former Ottoman war minister who had joined and then led the Basmachi dies in a cavalry charge against a Red Army machine-gun post.

title: Tajik ASSR created
description: Soviet national delimitation makes an autonomous Tajik republic inside Uzbekistan, the first Tajik state at all.

title: Gorno-Badakhshan autonomy
description: The Pamir peoples of the east get their own autonomous region within the Tajik republic.

title: Tajik SSR
description: Tajikistan becomes a full union republic with Khujand added to it, and its capital is renamed Stalinabad.

title: Khait earthquake
description: A magnitude-7.5 earthquake and its landslides bury villages in the Yasman valley and kill thousands, one of the Soviet era's worst disasters.

title: Stalinabad becomes Dushanbe
description: In the de-Stalinisation drive the capital takes back its old name, which means Monday, after its market day.

title: Nurek Dam completed
description: The 300-metre Nurek Dam on the Vakhsh, then the tallest dam in the world, is finished and still supplies most of Tajikistan's electricity.

title: Tajik made state language
description: A language law makes Tajik the republic's state language for the first time, a landmark in the national revival before independence.

title: Independence
description: Tajikistan declares independence from the collapsing Soviet Union, with ex-Communist Rahmon Nabiyev as its president.

title: Civil war begins
description: Demonstrations and counter-demonstrations in the capital spill into open war between the government and an Islamic-democratic opposition.

title: Nabiyev forced out
description: President Nabiyev resigns at gunpoint, but the war spreads through the south, and before the end of the year government forces are back in Dushanbe.

title: Peace accord
description: President Rahmon and opposition leader Nuri sign the agreement ending a civil war that killed tens of thousands and drove out a tenth of the people.

title: Somoni introduced
description: The somoni, named after the Samanid king Ismail, replaces the Tajik rouble as the national currency.

title: Anzob Tunnel opens
description: The Iranian-built tunnel through the Anzob Pass gives a year-round road between Dushanbe and Khujand, linking north and south without crossing Uzbekistan.

title: Sarazm World Heritage
description: The Bronze Age town site becomes Tajikistan's first UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Khorugh clashes
description: Government troops fight into Gorno-Badakhshan's capital after a security chief is killed, the worst violence in the Pamirs since the civil war.

title: Rogun Dam construction launched
description: President Rahmon launches construction of what is planned as the world's tallest dam, opposed by downstream Uzbekistan.
